Re-record only in the same commit as the change that moved it. ||| Re-recorded by the determinism-cliff pass, and this one is a re-record of the FORMAT rather than of the battle. Two things changed. (1) Two checkpoints added past t+200: the gate used to stop 5.5 s before the only cross-engine divergence anyone has measured (the field battle forks at t+205.5 s), so t+250 is the sentinel just past the fork and t+400 is the second half of the battle nothing had ever looked at. (2) Two new marks per checkpoint. `uf64` is the exact float64 bits of every continuous UnitGroupState field plus the waypoint queue — the layer the float32 pool hash cannot see, and which nothing in this repository hashed until now. `uctl` is the discrete half: order, target, formation, width, alive, kills, membership, flags, and unit array order. The five original pool hashes are UNCHANGED at all three battles across the whole pass, including across the Math.hypot -> Math.sqrt(a*a + b*b) substitution in the same branch, and so are all 21 survivor counts. Every `uf64` moved, and no `uctl` did: the substitution perturbs the simulation own float64 state everywhere, never reaches a control-flow decision, and never survives the float32 round trip. That is the quantisation firewall, and it is why the old five-checkpoint pool-only gate would have reported that a 222-call-site change did nothing. A `uf64` drift with `hash` and `uctl` unchanged is a PORTABILITY finding — a browser update is enough to cause one — and the gate warns rather than fails on it. A `uctl` or `hash` drift is a real change in the battle and still fails. Recorded from three independent page loads per battle, cross-checked against an earlier independent pair of runs: all 21 checkpoints reproduced exactly. Headcounts 8,632 / 3,074 / 3,440 confirm each arm measured the battle it names. ||| Re-recorded by the pass that put the field deployment on its own ground, and this one IS a re-record of the battle. `sim/scenario.ts` laid both lines out about x 0 and never read the deployment masks; §15 task 1 moved those masks east with the corrected Tiber and left the order of battle where it was, so at 70fc191 **747 of these 8,632 men were standing in the river** and another 412 were dry on the far bank, in the wrong battle. Measured with `tools/probe-ground.mjs --quality=high --views=none`, which now audits the men as well as the ground. The deployment is now translated once onto the axis the masks define — one shift of 271.146 m for every unit of both armies, so frontage (Rome 684.3 m, the host 783.4 m), spacing, width, facing, formation, unit count and headcount are identical to the metre before and after; only x moved. The battle that follows is a different battle for the obvious reason: an army that was fighting with its left wing in a river is not the same army. Survivors at t+400 move 5,217 -> 4,288. Measured at 70fc191 in a separate worktree, for the record: t+0 0fa6e702, then ee0f62b6, d343cc70, 3d79f110, 8ebc59fe, 7b951be2, 233e3022. Three things moved. (1) Both boxes were widened east with their **west edges pinned exactly where task 1 measured them against the Tiber** — the attacker's half-width 380 → 515 about cx 205 → 340, the defender's 250 → 425 about 205 → 380. (2) `standOnDeploymentGround` now insets its west anchor by the box's own feather, because the rectangle's edge is the contour where the mask reaches *zero*; that is 80 m of eastward shift, 271.146 → 351.146, one number for every unit of both armies. (3) `battleCoreMask` came off x 0 onto the deployment axis at a 745 m half-width, so the host's right wing is inside the damped corridor for the first time since task 1 (440 men were outside it). Measured by `tools/probe-ground.mjs --quality=high`: men outside their own box **562 Roman and 182 Juthungi → 0 and 0**, trees within 4 m of a man 1/4 → 0/0, worst slope under a man 0.315/0.048 → 0.074/0.076, in water 0 → 0, far bank 0 → 0. Survivors at t+400 move 4,288 → 4,660, which is what a battle fought on prepared instead of unprepared ground does. **The control is Carthage**, not this arm: `map=carthage&scenario=assault` is bit-identical across this tree at all seven checkpoints on `hash`, `uf64` and `uctl` at 3,440 men, and the shift on Carthage and on Pydna is still exactly 0.000 m (`tools/scratch/probe-standshift.mjs`). Worth writing down because the instruction for this pass got it the other way round: **`default` IS the Campus Martius field battle**, so it can never be a control for a change to that battle's deployment. A and B agree on every bit at all seven checkpoints here. One mark carries the whole "this is positioning, not balance" claim: **`uctl` at t+0 is still `2b2ac282`**, the value recorded at `88a4aa5` before the Tiber moved and before task 1 — the discrete half of every unit (order, target, formation, width, alive, kills, membership, flags, unit array order) is byte-identical to the battle that shipped. No simulation code was touched in this pass. On this arm — the shipped field battle, no city geometry — **t+0 and t+30 are byte-identical to the previous pin at `hash`, `uf64` and `uctl`**: the deployment ground under both boxes did not move, so the order of battle is placed identically and the first thirty seconds replay exactly. The first drift is t+90 and it is `uf64` only. It goes hard at t+150, once the wings have swung far enough west for the re-projected Tiber's bank to be under them. Survivors at t+400 rise from 4,660 to 5,175. Headcount 8,632, unchanged, which is how you know this arm is still the battle it names. ||| Re-recorded by the branch that assembled Rome (`e/city/rome-assembled`): phase 1, the Tiber re-survey, the landmark rework and its phase-3 follow-up in one tree for the first time. The field battle is fought on the Campus Martius and `campus-martius` builds the city in both scenarios, so this battle sees the re-surveyed channel AND the re-placed landmarks. Its t+30 hash is 3a315656 here against dc3fa068 pinned on main and 5903c5e0 pinned on e/terrain/tiber-resurvey -- a third value, not either input, which is consistent with it being the first tree to contain both changes. Head count unchanged at 8,632 in 35 units.

Re-recorded here for a movement that is NOT this pass's: cc72ea6 turned ROUGH_SLOWS_MOVEMENT on, published these exact five hashes in its own commit message -- t+0 unchanged at 22bb3df8, then e246f360, 326f06de, fe58e1f0, cedf0a10 -- and did not include this file in the commit, so the gate that exists to stop unannounced movement has been red on main ever since. The pass that recorded it changed the ram shed's cover test and moved nothing: 'default' and 'map=carthage&scenario=assault' are both bit-identical across it, and this entry's new hashes are cc72ea6's own. Re-record only in the same commit as the change that moved it. ||| Re-recorded again by the aperture pass, which is the change that moved it. Two mechanisms in src/sim/BattleSystem.ts reach this battle: fitToAperture squeezes a formation's frontage down to what the corridor ahead of it will take and spreads it back out once its tail is through, and aimRout deflects a broken unit's flight line round whatever it is about to run into. Both are inert on a map with no masonry on it, and the evidence is in this file: 'default' is bit-identical across the pass at all five checkpoints, and so are t+0 and t+30 of both assaults, which are before anything has routed or entered a gate. The drift starts at t+90 in both. Every reason a Rome battle can move applies at once here: KZ 0.222 -> 0.35, the Tiber rebuilt as a 451-station polyline with a signed distance field, resolveOverlaps deleted with every monument returned to its surveyed position, the Via Lata re-armatured round the Mausoleum of Augustus, and every district street restored after the merge silently dropped them. **Head count moved 3,074 -> 3,072 in 32 units**, because the defender count derives from the city's own garrison bays and the city changed. Note that `qa-determinism.mjs`'s own usage text still says 3,074; it is describing the phase-1 tree, not this one.
